Messages.Author: Jeff Endres
Messages.Body:
Recent talk about broken cards/combos has spurred me to write a comment. I
have been lurking for quite a while now, making occasional postings. I have
been out of the loop recently and have only just recently found out about
these recent RTR.

There are some good ideas and some bad ideas in the rulings. I will list
my _personal_ opinions on most of these and at the end of this post, state
a single small change which I think should be made.

I personally like the changes to Thoughts Betrayed, it's still a good card
and you can make some great combos with it, but there is now a reasonable
some reasonable defenses.

Heidelburg Castle, a good clear common sense _clarification_.

Zip Gun, A simple variation. Now a slightly useful card.

Directed Actions, *chuckle* Back to original? Fine.

Tomb of Ramses III. Ok variation. Although I would say reduce the cost to 2
pool since it is not permanent.

Golden Rule, a common sense and intelligent ruling. Unfortunately it falls
over because of previous other rulings. Stolen vamps loose their
disciplines, etc. because masters placed on them are still controlled by
the
original methuselah.

Aggravated Damage, either way is fine. I hear statements about how combat
decks are weaker but also complaints about how it is too easy to burn a
vampire. Aren't these complaints contradictory?

Fame, an interesting variant, but that is all. It could very well be a
completely new card. It makes a bunch of cool combos useless but opens up a
new bunch.

Mind Rape, a very weird rewrite. Mind Rape was a pretty cool card. Still
is, but there is now a new question about whether you _must_ burn the card
next turn or you must burn the card to get the effect... *chuckle* Need a
clarification on a rewrite of an otherwise clear card.

Pulled Fangs. Why? You now have two rulings which reduce burnings...

Return to Innocence. Now it is no longer blocked by Protected Resources or

Archon Investigation!!!! And it can't be bounced! So what does happen if

the card is burnt before the pool loss? Is the vampire still burnt? Is the
pool still lost?

Wake with Evening's Freshness. What!!! Why? To stop people cycling? This is
a very heavy restriction, and almost makes it wallpaper compared to Forced
Awakening.

-----------

Now for the major point of this post. Almost all these rules change the
game play quite significantly. Is this an alternative to releasing new
cards? Yes, it can be. But should it be official? I don't think so.
Especially when RTI is now even more powerful! Most of these rewrites
should be suggestions only.

A complete cleansing of the RTR would be good. Trying to _reduce_ the
number of significant rule changes and limit it to _errata_ and
clarifications. Specific rewrites of the game to make tournament games
fairly even should be available. Possibly numbering each possible rule
variant to allow an organizer to easily advertise in what way the game will
be played.

I am not saying this is the be all and end all solution but it is a better
idea than the collage of patches that is the current system.

Collage. A piece of art, yes, but is it beautiful?

--
Jeff Endres

Greetings Jeff.

> There are some good ideas and some bad ideas in the rulings. I will list
> my _personal_ opinions on most of these and at the end of this post, state
> a single small change which I think should be made.

> Golden Rule, a common sense and intelligent ruling. Unfortunately it falls

> over because of previous other rulings. Stolen vamps loose their
> disciplines, etc. because masters placed on them are still controlled by
> the original methuselah.

Well, as mentionned by LSJ, it doesn't "fall" over, tough I'll admit it
does
appear strange at first glance. But, we must remember that Disciplines are
"gifts" given by the Meth (you) to his minion (the vampire).

BTW, this rule about Discipline cards is generalized to other Master cards
except when Stolen or something like that (i.e. when the controller of the
card
has been explicitely changed). For instance, Anarch Troublemaker and
Millicent Smith explicitely allows the controller to be changed.

Others, like Curse of Nitocris and Society of Leopold (to name a few), are
always
*yours*, even when they are moving around the table. I wonder though if
they are also
burned when you are ousted (as well as when the condition on the card is
satisfied...)

> Mind Rape, a very weird rewrite. Mind Rape was a pretty cool card. Still
> is, but there is now a new question about whether you _must_ burn the card
> next turn or you must burn the card to get the effect... *chuckle* Need a
> clarification on a rewrite of an otherwise clear card.

>I am assuming that it is the first option, that is you must do it no

matter what,
>although the other is a valid interpretation especially for a beginner.

No offense intended, but it is a tendancy I have observed in myself and
others
(often without being noticed) to try to "twist" the meaning of the words on
a card
to find another meaning that satisfies us. I've done it often, and will do
it again;
but I always try to check either I'm trying to see something that ain't
there, because
I need to see it there. :-(

One must always remember that we must read these cards using the common
signification for the words, and the sentences they are in (all the while
remembering the basic rules, if required). This is not a game played by
lawers, please.
So, must is must; no option available. May or can gives an option.

> Now for the major point of this post. Almost all these rules change the
> game play quite significantly. Is this an alternative to releasing new
> cards? Yes, it can be. But should it be official? I don't think so.
> Especially when RTI is now even more powerful! Most of these rewrites
> should be suggestions only.

They are always suggestions. As mentionned numerous times in other tread,
you can play with the (house) rules you wish. And it will be all right.
Much the same about the law, and how it is applied inside each of our
respective "private" houses.

However, when meeting with other players from outside our circle, we must
agree
on a common set of rules so that everyone can understand each other, and
deal
on the same level.

> fairly even should be available. Possibly numbering each possible rule
> variant to allow an organizer to easily advertise in what way the game will
> be played.

Could be interesting. But, I don't thing it would be better to get into a
tournament
knowing that Combat rule 12.5 is applied, with ActionMod/Reaction 2.1 and
RTI fix 3.7, etc. It would mess up most players (and the judges! :).

As someone else mentionned, one of the purposes of tournaments
is to compete with others in our environment, but also to compare with
others in
other tournament (with the point system in development). If everyone uses
different rules, how are you going to make a valid comparison between
different
tournaments?

> I am not saying this is the be all and end all solution but it is a better
> idea than the collage of patches that is the current system.
>
> Collage. A piece of art, yes, but is it beautiful?

One's appreciation of Art, as with many things, depends on your point
of view, your past experiences, your knowledge, etc..

Frederic.

This has to do with the control of master cards, not the new/old version
of the Golden Rule.

Try this:

Meth B steals Meth A's vampire. Meth B plays a skill card on the vamp.
Meth C steals the vamp from Meth B.

Under the old or new rules, if Meth B is ousted, the skill card (being
controlled by B) is burned while the vampire itself is not.

Under the old rules, if Meth A is ousted the vampire is burned, even though
Meth C had nothing to do with Meth A - he stole the vampire from Meth B.

The part about confusing "must" with "may" should've answered the question.
To reiterate, the answer is: "must means must".
It says "during [her] next minion phase, she must", therefore during her
next minion phase, she must.

> I see the major point of my post is not addressed. Why not? Please respond,

restricted to a tournament setting. Futher, piecemealling the rulings
to make a sort of 'a la carte' tournament system defeats the whole
process of tournament ratings.

Archon Investigation is broken because the benefit is amazingly good
for the cost (a master phase action) and the swing effect is tremedous.
You risk very little, and someone else loses a vampire.
Essentially, AI could be reworded as a 0 cost M:OoT card, saying,
"reduce a bleed greater than 3 to 3. Burn the bleeding minion." There's
no risk to playing it (even a DI or SI will leave you in no worse position
than you would have been if you hadn't played it) but someone else loses
a vampire.
(There's also the secondary issue that AI doesn't hose pure S&B deck,
like everyone thinks it does, since (as you point out) they can bleed
consistently for smaller amounts. Of course, Tap & Bleed decks, and
Bruise & Bleed decks usually only get 1 bleed through in a turn, and
at considerable risk to themselves. But hey, Jyhad will be a much better
game if everyone's deck includes Dom, Aus, and AI, won't it?)
Protected Resources is a bit more iffy... but I think there is something
*wrong* with a card that costs nothing to play, hoses an entire strategy,
and cannot be removed except by the controller's actions (and can't be
stolen, either). If there were a card (Hidden Bunker, say?) that cost
nothing
and said "Your minions do not go to torpor when they take aggravated damage
and cannot take more than 3 points of damage in combat. Burn this card if
any of minions ever inflict 3 or more points of damage as a strike" then I
think everyone would agree that was broken, yes? Protected Resources
works about the same.

>that not acceptable Jimmy?

Not really. If your predator is a bleed deck, they'll push the 3-bleed
envelope pretty often. If not, just discard it. Besides which, when
the card is played, it has a negative cost. Any other "cost" it might
have only serves to bring it closer to "free".

> Risks and uncertainty are what make Jyhad great. Stop looking for the 100%
> effective deck, there is none.

But combat should be (and is, barring RtI and such) a viable bleed
defense.

> I remember playing a Gangrel combat/small bleed deck vs a similar Brujah

> pulled out a RTI. "Ah ha. I've got you now." I thought. I waited a turn to

So he hosed your trump card with an anti-trump trump card. Wouldn't the
game have been a lot better without _either_ of these cards?

[Protracted Racehorses]
> Costs nothing? A Master that costs 2 pool and stops you from bleeding?

Costs you 2 pool, but if you're even playing it, it will save you many
times over that much. And many decks don't need to bleed to kill you.
This card just isn't necessary; it was most likely crafted out of an
imaginary fear of heavy bleed decks. But we don't need bleed-hoser
cards to deal with bleed decks, and their existence isn't good for the
game. I'll be honest with you; when these cards (PR, AI, etc.) first
came out, I was happy. I was sick of getting killed by stupid bleed
decks. But once I learned to put bleed defense into my decks, and learn
how to keep myself from getting killed so easily, I realized that these
cards are unnecessary, and simply too powerful.

are considered horrendously stupid strategy, and will only be used in the
last seconds of a losing game. They connect approximately 5% of the time and

+X, where X is equal to this vampire's capacity. The acting vampire may play
no action modifiers until the end of this action, and may not use any effect
which would make this action unblockable. After combat, or after the action
is successful (whichever is appropriate), burn the acting vampire." THEN it
would be similar to a Hail Mary. Since it doesn't say that, it's a faulty

consider the card fundamentally broken. Just a bit overpowered and f#@%ing
annoying. I advocate banning it in tournaments, but leaving it as is
otherwise.

> > If there were a card (Hidden Bunker, say?) that cost
> > nothing
> > and said "Your minions do not go to torpor when they take aggravated damage
> > and cannot take more than 3 points of damage in combat. Burn this card if

> > think everyone would agree that was broken, yes? Protected Resources
> > works about the same.

> like:
> Your minions cannot take more than 3 points of damage per _strike_
> in combat. Burn this card if your minions inflict agravated damage
> or more than 1 point of damage in combat.
>

That's still horribly broken (and I don't honestly think PR is as broken as
this card... but it's sort of a toss-up). And note that Protected Resources
limits it to 2 pool per action, so "per combat" is probably more analogous.

-Chris

Messages.Author: Bernie Bresnahan
Messages.Body:
I've been pretty silent on the whole RTI thing, but I'm pretty much
in full agreement with James (gak!).

Here's how I got ousted in the finals at Origins 97'.
My deck was Malkavian Anti-Tribue, all Sabbat cards.

On approximately my 4th turn my predator announced that
his new Inner Circle (Etrius I think) was going to bleed me
with RTI.
I attempted to block, he put stealth on it.
I played a Misdirection to my Prey.
My Prey uses a Direct Intervention on my Misdirection.
Etrius increases his bleed for a total of 16 bleed.
I'm at -1 pool and ousted from the game, tied for 3rd place.

Opinion: The best reasonable fix I've heard in recent
discussion is that Action Mods. cannot be used with
RTI. It would be a lot easier explain and discuss with
my playgroup than the current re-wording of 7/7.

Divine Intervention: Do I feel hosed by this card? Not
really. My complaint with DI is in it's extreme versatility.
It's cost comes off about right otherwise. I proposed a
fix for this earlier, which nobody commented on.

On a last note, I'm a bit suprised that nobody mentioned
pack tactics or elder intervention (the clanless 2 cards
that give you +2 intercept vs. bleeds). Just wanted to
point out that Auspex isn't absolutely necessary to
intercept a bleed.

Bernie Bresnahan

This initial proposition came out when Ancient Hearts was first released,
and I can't remember the conclusion we arrived at.

> Divine Intervention: Do I feel hosed by this card? Not
> really. My complaint with DI is in it's extreme versatility.
> It's cost comes off about right otherwise. I proposed a
> fix for this earlier, which nobody commented on.

I think that the best fix I've seen is the "Giant's Blood" fix:

Append to the text: Direct Intervention is only playable once per game.
(I.e., it is unique amongst ALL the Meths). This makes the cost of the
card increase dramatically (your card can easily become a wasted
deckspace slot)).

> On a last note, I'm a bit suprised that nobody mentioned
> pack tactics or elder intervention (the clanless 2 cards
> that give you +2 intercept vs. bleeds). Just wanted to
> point out that Auspex isn't absolutely necessary to
> intercept a bleed.

Well, if a deck is not an intercept deck, Elder Intervention and pack
tactics are not that useful. You simply do NOT want to block a Stealth
deck if you are not an intercept deck. By not blocking, you clog the
stealth Meth with stealth cards in hand, and they cannot cycle. +2
intercept is simply not enough to block a stealth bleeder. You will
simply exercise their hand and waste your own time. You need EXTREME
multiple copies in order to be able to drain all of their stealth.

Simply put, those cards are not effective, in general.
